messages:
Anya: heads-up — found an odd attribute-routing edge-case in the canary. When a request has both an org-scoped API key and a project-bound key attached via proxy, the routing fallback sometimes attributes to the org instead of the project. This skews per-project quotas in the console and makes the project dashboard show lower usage than reality. :thinking:
Sam: ugh. is this only when the project key is ephemeral or missing some header? any repro steps?
Anya: repro is pretty simple — send a request with headers:
```
Authorization: ApiKey org:ORG_ID:keyabcd
X-Project-Key: proj:PROJECT_ID:xyz
```
runtime currently checks order-of-parsing and falls back to the first valid principal it sees. because the proxy injects the org auth earlier, we pick org.
Miguel: that explains the quota misattribution in last night's spike. infra alert showed project quota breaches while console showed org-level consumption. can we add tags to telemetry to distinguish both resolved principals?
Anya: yep. proposal: change routing heuristic to prefer explicit project-scoped keys over org-scoped when both present. fallback order: project > service_account > org. Also emit both resolved_principal and fallback_candidate tags to tracing/metrics.
Sam: prefer project-by-default sounds safe, but two follow-ups: 1) are there any downstream caches that key-by-org currently prime? we don't want cache poisoning. 2) what about delegated keys where service-account is proxying for a project?
Anya: good call. For caches, we'd include a cache-key variant that encodes resolved scope: e.g., `cache_key = v1|{model}|{resolved_scope_type}:{id}`. That avoids mixing org-primed entries into project caches. For delegation, if SA indicates acting_on_project claim, treat that as project-scoped. Otherwise use SA ordering.
Miguel: agree on cache namespacing. For telemetry, let's add two new tags: `auth.attribution` (project|org|sa|ambiguous) and `auth.candidate_chain` (comma list). That should let dashboards surface every ambiguous case without changing existing panels.
Rebecca: from product POV — we need to avoid surprising customers. If we flip heuristics, projects might see suddenly higher usage. How do we communicate? Canary + opt-in flag first? Also UX: show an 'attribution change' banner on affected project dashboards for 24–48h. :sparkles:
Anya: plan: roll feature behind runtime flag `prefer_project_attribution`. Canary enabled for 5% of traffic for 48h, emit telemetry, compare project-level billing delta. If delta matches expectation, flip to 100% and show console banner with link to docs explaining behavior.
Sam: add unit tests for header parsing order and cache namespace. Also add integration test that simulates delegated SA acting_on_project.
Miguel: I'll wire a Grafana panel for `auth.attribution` breakdown and an alert when ambiguous ratio > 5% in canary.
InfraBot: deploy-canary started by @miguel — canary id: cny-2026-03-21-57, targets subset 5% traffic in us-west1. Logs will be forwarded to #build-failures.
Anya: awesome. I'll open a tiny console PR for the banner + telemetry toggle in the admin flags page. Rebecca — can you draft the short banner copy?
Rebecca: sure — will post a draft in #product-review in a bit. Keep it short: "Attribution update: we've improved how requests are attributed between org/project keys. You may see supressed/ increased project usage during the migration window. Learn more."
Sam: let's also add a hidden metric in staging that simulates older behavior so we can run diff tests in CI.
Anya: ok filed a tracking ticket: infra/attr-routing-2026. I'll push the runtime flag PR and tests today. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:
